newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell unit will not extend Air Force pact.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell unit will not extend Air Force pact.

text.p: Zenith Data Systems said Friday it and the U.S. Air Force have agreed not to extend a contract calling for Zenith to provide the agency with personal computer hardware and support services.
The contract was worth as much $1 billion, said Jeremy Kehoe, a spokesman for Zenith, a division of closely held Packard Bell NEC.

It was awarded jointly to Zenith and Hughes Data Systems, a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp and the decision means the pact will end this month rather than extending through another two option years, Kehoe said.
A statement from Zenith said the Air Force may still statisfy its needs through the Hughes contract.
Kehoe said Zenith had successfully resolved certain delivery issues under the contract, but that both sides agreed it was best not to extend the pact.
Zenith General Manager Jim Shea said Zenith received $100 million in revenues to date from the contract and will continue to sell to the Air Force and other defense agencies through other contracts.
